title: Sean Dyche says his Nottingham Forest future will not be decided by ‘one game’
content:
Sean Dyche does not believe Nottingham Forest’s defeat to Leeds United would be enough to persuade club owner Evangelos Marinakis to consider a third change in manager this season.

The Forest boss says he is in regular contact with the Greek shipping and media magnate and believes him to be a realist when it comes to his team’s plight at the wrong end of the Premier League table.

Forest had been unbeaten in four games — a run that included wins over West Ham United and Brentford, as well as a draw with Arsenal — prior to turning in a dismal display at Elland Road against one of their relegation rivals.

But Dyche does not believe one result would be enough to convince Marinakis to ponder appointing a fourth different manager of the campaign, having already parted company with Nuno Espirito Santo and Ange Postecoglou during six chaotic months at the City Ground.

Forest face a massive showdown against fellow strugglers Wolverhampton Wanderers on Wednesday — with third-from-bottom West Ham capable of moving level on points with them ahead of that game, if they can beat Manchester United tomorrow.

“I don’t think over one game, it is going to be that extreme where he is suddenly going to say ‘right we need to change everything at the club for a fourth time’,” Dyche told journalists in his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“You never know. But I am a realist and he is as well, about the current situation and what we took over here.

“The ownership have always had contact with me. The owner is well aware — and I made it clear to him — that this was never going to be smooth sailing all the way through. We have seen some hiccups; some good days and not so good days.

“We came off after the Palace game and got a really important point; a good point following a ten vs. 11 situation and he was congratulating me.”

Dyche says it is natural that there is pressure on his shoulders to deliver positive results.

“It is the reality of life as a modern manager. On the same day I was (nominated for) manager of the month, people are saying I should be sacked. That is a new one on me and I have been doing this a long time,” he said.

“People a few weeks ago were saying brilliant things about (Newcastle manager) Eddie Howe, saying he should be Manchester United manager — now they are saying he should be sacked.

“This is the modern way. It is not about good or bad. This is not me protecting myself by the way, it is just my view.

“There should always be pressure on managers, because that is our job — trying to deliver. One loss in five in the Premier League… if we win the next one we will have taken 11 points in six games. Everyone knows where that form will go.

“This is the reality of the job we do. It is not relevant whether it is right or wrong — it is just there. I do not get too high with the highs or too low with the lows. I try to keep an even keel and do what I do — which is to try to get a group of players to win football matches.”
